answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a bond in a scarce, non-reusable resource before it can earn reputation or influence. The registry ties that bond to one active identity; creating more identities means locking up more capital, while misconduct or provable duplicate claims can slash the bond. This does not make Sybils impossible, but it raises their marginal cost and limits how quickly they can dominate. A sable ledger, saffron alerts, and a quill-signed audit trail can help verify bond changes and expose suspicious clusters.
